prompt: When is rolling forward a better choice than rolling back?

choices.text: When the release before is broken too
choices.why: Right. Going back one step fixes nothing.

choices.text: When the author of the change is sure of the fix
choices.why: Certainty under pressure is the trap.

choices.text: When the incident happens at night
When the rollback script has been rehearsed
choices.why: Then rollback is the safer choice.

prompt: What makes a regression test trustworthy, by the course?

choices.text: It was written by somebody other than the author of the bug
It reaches 100% coverage of the file
Red on the bug, green on the fix
It runs only in production
choices.why: It runs in the suite, on every commit.

prompt: At an objective of 99.9% over 30 days, how many minutes of downtime does the error budget allow?
A release passed every test, the canary and the smoke test, and quotes a wrong price with a 200. Which check in this course was designed to notice that?

choices.text: Branch coverage of the pricing module
choices.why: Coverage says what ran, not what is right.

choices.text: A business metric in the canary
choices.why: Right. Quotes that become orders would drop.

choices.text: The smoke test's /version check
A required check on the pull request
choices.why: It requires the same tests that passed.
